newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close sharply up, BNI listing looms.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close sharply up, BNI listing looms.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended 1.64 percent up on Friday ahead of the listing of giant Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) on the back of bargain-hunting and fresh buying in some big-caps, brokers said.

They said many investors were coming into the market after receiving refunds from unsuccessful bids in the BNI public offer and had focused on blue-chips including Astra International, Barito Pacific and Bimantara Citra.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 9.87 points, or 1.64 percent to close at 612.86 points after hitting an intra-day high of 614.52 points in late trading.
Gainers led losers by 63 to 45, with 58 counters unchanged.
"The market is likely to be more active in the coming week, enlivened by the listing of BNI," said Motoo Murata, resident senior economist of the Daiwa Institute of Research.

Murata said some bank stocks could enjoy a spillover effect from the BNI offer because many unsuccessful investors could pick the stock up in the secondary market. "They could also pick up other bank stocks," he added.
Brokers said bargain-hunting on Telkom and Gudang Garam coupled with fresh buying of Astra International and some medium-sized stocks had pushed the index up sharply.
Timber firm Barito Pacific topped the active list with 30.8 million shares traded, rising 225 rupiah to 1,575 after reaching a high of 1,625 rupiah.
Brokers ascribed the rise to talk of a possible take-over by prominent businessmen. Barito Pacific spokesman Steve Beck denied the rumours.
"Maybe brokers just realise that Barito Pacific's price is undervalued," he added.
Heavyweight Telkom rose 50 rupiah to 3,850 on a volume of 4.3 million shares despite a fall in New York overnight.
Blue-chip Astra International rose 9.89 percent to 5,000 rupiah from 4,550 on a volume of 3.1 million shares on good fundamentals.
Seasoning producer Miwon Indonesia rose 150 rupiah to 3,675 on a volume of 12.7 million shares.
Brokers said it was due to fundamentals coupled with speculation that the firm could be considering a stock split.
Food and beverage Suba Indah was also actively traded, rising 175 rupiah to 2,300 on a turnover of 3.7 million shares on what brokers said was due to talk of another company buying into the firm.
Company officials were not available for comment.
Conglomerate Bimantara Citra rose 150 rupiah to 3,300 on a turnover of 1.6 million shares on fresh buying, brokers said.
